title: Complementary p-basis monomial linearIndependent
statement:
Let p be prime and k a field of characteristic p [def-weil-field]. Let I be any index type and t : I → k. Assume that the bounded finitely supported monomials in t form a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of k over F_p(k^p), precisely as expressed by hpb below. Let J be a finite subset of I and kJ the subfield generated by all pth powers and all t_i with i outside J, precisely as expressed by hkJ below. Then the bounded J-monomials are linearly independent over kJ. Complete formal statement: theorem pBasisComplementMonomialBasis_linearIndependent
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (I : Type w) (t : I → k)
    (hpb : ∃ b : Module.Basis
      {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}
      (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p))) k,
      ∀ E, b E = (E : I →₀ ℕ).prod (fun i e ↦ t i ^ e))
    (J : Finset I) (kJ : Subfield k)
    (hkJ : kJ = Subfield.closure
      (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p) ∪ {x : k | ∃ i : I, i ∉ J ∧ t i = x})) :
    LinearIndependent kJ (fun E : J → Fin p ↦ ∏ i : J, t i ^ (E i : ℕ))

proof.text: Apply the complementary monomial span theorem to each kJ coefficient. Only containment of kJ in that span is needed; the identification of F with the Frobenius image and the reverse containment are unnecessary.

Zero-extend each J → Fin p exponent function to I using Finsupp.onFinset. Add a bounded complementary exponent function. On J the result recovers the J exponents; outside J it recovers the complementary exponents, so this pairing map is injective and remains bounded. Finsupp.prod_add_index and prod_onFinset identify the paired products with the corresponding original basis monomials. Compose the original basis independence with the injective pairing map.

For a finite kJ-linear relation, expand each coefficient in the complementary span as a finitely supported F-linear combination. Let U be the union of the supports over the finite relation support S. Distribute the relation into an F-linear relation indexed by S × U among the independent paired monomials. Every expanded coefficient vanishes. Outside U the coefficients vanish by their support property. The original coefficient expansions therefore show every kJ coefficient is zero, proving linear independence.
